frozen_candidate_root_contribution: The outer bounding rim/verge of the visible spatial expanse — the far encompassing edge where the seen field terminates (the "horizon"), conceived as the outermost perimeter of the observable world.

internal_discovery.candidate_root_contribution: The outer bounding rim/verge of the visible spatial expanse — the far encompassing edge where the seen field terminates (the "horizon"), conceived as the outermost perimeter of the observable world.
internal_discovery.plain_explanation: All three occurrences are the same noun (QAC tag N), the horizon-word, in two morphological shapes: the plural ٱلْـَٔافَاق (41:53) and the singular ٱلْأُفُق (53:7; 81:23). In 41:53, "We will show them Our signs فِى ٱلْـَٔافَاق (in the horizons/outer regions) وَفِىٓ أَنفُسِهِمْ (and in themselves)" — the āfāq are explicitly set OPPOSITE the inner self (anfus), so the root here contributes the OUTER encompassing expanse/verge of the world, the far bounding regions, as against the interior. In 53:7 "وَهُوَ بِٱلْأُفُقِ ٱلْأَعْلَىٰ (and he was at the highest ufuq/horizon)" and 81:23 "وَلَقَدْ رَءَاهُ بِٱلْأُفُقِ ٱلْمُبِينِ (he saw him at the clear ufuq/horizon)", the singular ufuq is the horizon-edge on which a figure appears/is seen — the outer rim of the visual field where sky meets the limit of sight. Across the plural "outer regions/horizons" and the singular "horizon-rim where a figure is beheld," the invariant is the same: the outermost bounding verge of the visible expanse. Subtracting the qualifiers (ٱلْأَعْلَىٰ "highest", ٱلْمُبِين "clear/manifest") and the pluralization leaves exactly this bounding-outer-edge notion.
internal_discovery.layer_separation_note: FORM: all three are nominal (N); the only derivational variation is number — plural ٱلْـَٔافَاق vs singular ٱلْأُفُق. The plural morphology supplies multiplicity/spread ("regions, quarters"); subtracting it leaves the singular notion "horizon-verge." No verbal/participial/passive layer to strip. CONSTRUCTION: locative prepositions — فِى ("in/within", 41:53) and بِ ("at/on", 53:7; 81:23) supply the "located-in/at" vector; subtract that, the root itself is not the location-relation but the place-type (bounding rim). The determiner ٱل and the attributive adjectives ٱلْأَعْلَىٰ / ٱلْمُبِين supply height and clarity externally; subtract. PARTICIPANTS: the shown signs (āyāt) in 41:53, the beheld figure in 53:7/81:23 — irrelevant to the root residue. CONTEXT: cosmic-sign discourse (41:53) vs revelatory-vision narrative (53:7; 81:23); both drop out. Residue after subtraction = the outer encompassing edge/verge of the visible expanse.
internal_discovery.strongest_counterexample: 41:53 (word_ref 41:53:4:2), the plural ٱلْـَٔافَاق. It is the hardest case because, contrasted with أَنفُسِهِمْ ("their selves"), it can read as "the whole outer world/cosmos" broadly rather than narrowly "the horizon-rim," tempting a wider "external world" gloss. It reconciles cleanly: the plural of ufuq is precisely the far outer horizons/regions that bound and encompass the world; the outer-vs-inner contrast (āfāq vs anfus) actually confirms the root's "outer encompassing verge" contribution rather than defeating it. The extension from "edge" to "outer regions" is the ordinary semantic effect of pluralizing a boundary-rim noun, not a different root sense.
internal_discovery.competing_hypothesis: The strongest alternative core is "the sky / heavenly upper region" (i.e., Afq ≈ celestial zone). It fits 53:7 ("highest") and 81:23 (a figure seen aloft) superficially. But internal evidence arbitrates against it: in 41:53 the plural āfāq denotes the outer horizons of the world set opposite the inner self, not specifically the heavens; and the "highness" in 53:7 comes from the explicit adjective ٱلْأَعْلَىٰ, not from the root — if ufuq inherently meant "sky," "highest ufuq" would be near-redundant, whereas as "horizon-edge" the qualifier "highest/uppermost" is informative. A second alternative, "distance/remoteness," is weaker: horizon is a visible bounding edge, not mere farness, and the āfāq/anfus outer-vs-inner axis is about perimeter/exteriority, not distance. The bounding-outer-verge reading covers all three without strain.
internal_discovery.distinctiveness_note: Nearest semantic neighbors: (1) smw (س م و) "sky/heaven, elevation" — a region/substance overhead; Afq differs by naming not the overhead region but the encircling EDGE of the visible field where the expanse terminates. (2) Hdd (ح د د) "limit/boundary" — an abstract or measured/legal terminus; Afq is specifically the VISIBLE far verge of a perceptual expanse, tied to sight, not a decreed or numeric limit. (3) bEd / nAy "distance, remoteness" — mere farness without an edge; Afq contributes an actual bounding rim, and its contrast with anfus (inner) marks exteriority/perimeter, not distance. Falsifiability: if a confirmed Afq occurrence denoted an interior locus, a non-visual abstract limit, or "sky as substance/region" with no sense of an outer bounding verge, the "visible outer encompassing edge" residue would fail.
internal_discovery.rationale: The root surfaces in only one lexical shape (the horizon-noun) across all three occurrences, and the invariant "outer bounding verge of the visible expanse" is directly recoverable at the surface in each: the singular ufuq as the horizon-rim where a figure is beheld (53:7; 81:23) and the plural āfāq as the outer encompassing regions of the world set against the inner self (41:53). The direction is determinate (outer/perimeter, tied to visibility), and the contribution is sharply distinct from sky (smw), abstract limit (Hdd), and mere distance (bEd) — the deciding internal cues being the āfāq/anfus outer-vs-inner contrast and the fact that height/clarity are supplied by external adjectives, not the root. No occurrence resists the residue; none is forced. The only inferential step is the ordinary edge→outer-regions widening carried by pluralization, which is internally bridged rather than a distinct sense, so unity is robust and strong.

adversarial_verification.notes: All 3 occurrences are the same noun (QAC tag N), the horizon-word ufuq/afaq, from root a-f-q. Tried hard to refute; found no genuine failing occurrence. 53:7 (al-ufuq al-a'la, "highest horizon") and 81:23 (al-ufuq al-mubin, "clear horizon") are the singular sky-horizon edge on which the beheld figure appears — a precise match to the candidate's "outer rim/verge where sky meets the limit of sight." Hardest case: 41:53 plural al-afaq, set opposite anfusihim ("themselves"). Standard reading is "the outer REGIONS/reaches of the world" — an area/expanse rather than a thin terminating edge-line, so the candidate's "rim/verge/outermost perimeter" framing is slightly narrow here. Resolution: the plural of "horizon" naturally metonymizes to "the far regions out toward the horizons," and the invariant (outermost bounding verge of the visible expanse) still underlies it; this is ordinary singular-edge / plural-far-regions polysemy within one root, not a semantic split or homonymy. No occurrence carries any unrelated sense (no proper-name or "ease" homonym), so the unity holds. Distinctiveness vs neighbors is adequate: distinct from janb (side/flank), nawahi (regions generically), sama' (sky), and bu'd (farness) because ufuq specifically names the visual terminating edge where sky meets sight. Falsifiable: a non-horizon occurrence would break it, but none exists. The rim-vs-regions nuance is a framing quibble the invariant bridges, not a genuine defect — hence SUPPORTED rather than PARTIALLY.

occurrence_dispositions.note: Plural ٱلْـَٔافَاقِ 'in the horizons/outer regions', explicitly opposed to وَفِىٓ أَنفُسِهِمْ ('in themselves'); the āfāq denote the outer bounding expanse of the world versus the interior — exactly the outermost-verge residue after subtracting pluralization.
Singular ٱلْأُفُقِ qualified by ٱلْأَعْلَىٰ ('highest'): the horizon-rim on which the figure is; subtracting the 'highest' qualifier leaves the bounding outer edge of the visual field.
Singular ٱلْأُفُقِ with ٱلْمُبِينِ ('clear/manifest') in رَءَاهُ ('he saw him'): the horizon-edge where a beheld figure appears; subtracting 'clear' leaves the same outermost visible verge.
